discovery: Prediction and discovery of near-room-temperature superconductivity in compressed hydrogen-rich compounds
subfield: Condensed matter physics - superconductivity at extreme pressure
motivation: Ashcroft's old idea that hydrogen-dominated metals should superconduct at very high temperatures became a quantitative, falsifiable theory through first-principles crystal-structure prediction. Duan and Ma predicted superconductivity near 200 K in compressed H3S, and Ma's group predicted clathrate superhydrides such as CaH6 and LaH10. These specific predictions were then confirmed: H3S at 203 K (2015), and LaH10 above 250 K, where Hemley's group gave one of the first demonstrations (2018-2019). Large isotope effects, Meissner and flux-trapping evidence, and independent replications show conventional phonon-mediated pairing at temperatures once thought impossible. This work overturned the textbook view that electron-phonon superconductivity is limited to low temperatures. It also made computational materials prediction a reliable discovery tool and opened a new field of superhydrides. Mikhail Eremets, whose experiments were central, has sadly died; these living nominees carry the decisive theoretical and experimental contributions.
